speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand your infant is suffering from bilious vomiting and has not passed meconium, causing abdominal distension. This combination of symptoms is very concerning. To begin my assessment, is the baby currently in the first week of life, and do you know their exact birth weight and gestational age?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-day-old male infant. The infant was born via a home birth without complications. The mother reports that the infant has had bilious vomiting and has not been able to pass meconium since birth. She also notes that the infant's abdomen appears distended.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Distal Intestinal Obstruction, likely Hirschsprung's disease or Distal Intestinal Obstruction Syndrome (DIOS). The clinical presentation of bilious vomiting, failure to pass meconium, and abdominal distension in a 2-day-old is highly suggestive of a distal intestinal obstruction. Immediate evaluation with an abdominal X-ray and rectal examination is recommended to confirm the diagnosis.
